goal: Decide if a string is a well-formed kappa-label, the content address every kappa-distribution object is named by, before anything trusts it.

app.name: kappa-label-check
app.title: Kappa-label check
app.purpose: Decide, as an XACML policy decision, whether a candidate kappa-label is admitted, from its sigma-axis token, the number of colons, whether its digest is lowercase hex, and how many hex digits it carries.
limits: It does not hash content; it decides whether the label's form is one the spec admits.
The ASCII range check on every byte is done by the parser that splits the label into these fields.

fields.name: axis
fields.means: the sigma-axis token before the colon

fields.name: colons
fields.means: how many colons the label holds

fields.name: hex
fields.means: whether every digest character is 0-9 or a-f

fields.name: digits
fields.means: how many hex digits follow the colon

meanings.permit: a well-formed kappa-label under a recognized sigma-axis
meanings.deny: rejected: construction is fallible and the label violates a constraint
meanings.not-applicable: no field of the label applies; never answered for a parsed label
meanings.indeterminate: the label could not be parsed into fields; never answered for a parsed label

rules.why: KAPPA_DISTRIBUTION_SPEC_v2.md 3.2: exactly one colon separator exists
KAPPA_DISTRIBUTION_SPEC_v2.md 3.2: exactly one colon separator exists
3.2: the suffix is entirely lowercase hexadecimal digits
3.2: sha512 has 64 digest bytes, so 128 hex digits
3.2: sha256, blake3, sha3-256 and keccak256 have 32 digest bytes, so 64 hex digits

app.otherwiseWhy: 3.2: the hex digit count equals twice the digest byte count for the token

properties.why: an unrecognized sigma-axis is never admitted
an uppercase or non-hex digest is never admitted
no admitted label is shorter than 32 digest bytes

stakeholders.name: Platform engineer
stakeholders.text: Builds the internal platform and its golden paths, and needs one honest verdict that a registry speaks kappa-distribution before teams depend on it.

stakeholders.name: Security engineer
stakeholders.text: Owns supply-chain integrity and needs every address the platform trusts to be one the spec admits, refused otherwise.

concerns.name: Only spec-admitted addresses
concerns.text: A content address with an unknown algorithm, the wrong length or a non-hex digest is refused, never guessed.

threats.name: Algorithm confusion
threats.text: A label names an unrecognized or weaker axis so a different digest is accepted for the same name.

control.name: Closed axis set
control.text: Only the five sigma-axis tokens are admitted, each with its exact digit count, proved for every request.

components.name: Prism page
components.text: The published GitHub Pages site: it checks the holo seal, sends the request to the verified guest in the browser and shows the answer in the reader's view.

components.name: Pipeline adapter
components.text: The CI step that sends the same request line to the same holo and fails the pipeline on the answer, so a pipeline and a person get one answer.

quality.text: No kappa-label outside the spec grammar is permitted.
quality.measureText: Requests with an unknown axis, uppercase hex or too few digits answered permit.
